gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI MultiCooler, a wheeled 42 qt compressor cooler with its own LFP battery, is $569 at BLUETTI's US store today (list $699), nearly $200 less than the cut-price EcoFlow GLACIER Classic 55L ($849), while GearJunkie still lists the MultiCooler at $699 and the gift-guide pages give no prices at all.
standout_why: Compared against GearJunkie (2026-10-31), giftsitter.com and lovethe88.com (wheels list). GearJunkie prices its battery coolers at $699 (BLUETTI MultiCooler), $800 (Anker SOLIX EverFrost 2 40) and $500 (BougeRV CRD45, battery $200 extra). None of those is today's store price. Giftsitter and lovethe88 show no prices, only 'Check Price On Amazon', and say nothing about battery capacity. Neither of those two lists the MultiCooler, EverFrost 2 or GLACIER Classic. Car and Driver blocked fetching, so I could not compare it.
decides: ChatGPT's four cards ($227–$320) are all plug-in models. Its own advice tells the shopper to pick a battery model to cool away from outlets but never shows one. Today's store prices put a wheeled cooler with a battery and a compressor at $569 (BLUETTI MultiCooler) against GearJunkie's $800 for the Anker EverFrost 2 40. That moves 'wheels + battery' from the $400+ bracket to the low end of it. It confirms the MultiCooler as the value pick for 'rolls and runs with no outlet'. The EverFrost 2 (our product) has to win on its removable 288 Wh battery and 6-inch wheels, not on price, and I could not read its US price today.
